content: This is the discussion thread for #General announcements > Lean on Compiler Explorer
It would be amazing if the Lean IR could also be displayed side-by-side!

Is setting trace.compiler.ir.result and then reading stdout the way to get the IR?

Note that you can use set_option in the source code, and then see the full compiler output by clicking on "Output" at the bottom of the assembly pane.

It would be nice to have a dedicated option and pane for Lean IR but I'm not sure how to accurately parse it out of the compiler output.
You'd want to use trace.Compiler.result nowadays. You could both parse it or run a lean meta program to extract the IR directly in some format you like
Would it make sense to also expose the LLVM mode of the lean compiler here?

Eric Wieser said:

Would it make sense to also expose the LLVM mode of the lean compiler here?

If you want to sure, though it's rather unmaintained at the moment and CI doesn't even guarantee it will work.
@Francisco Giordano how interested are you in keeping the godbolt integration up to date with our monthly releases? Or should this be something we do as we release?
I also wonder whether it would be possible to have some compiler flag presets? E.g. basically everything is compiled with -O3 -DNDEBUG

Henrik Böving said:

Francisco Giordano how interested are you in keeping the godbolt integration up to date with our monthly releases?

Yeah I think I can do this. Let me start by updating to the latest and see what that's like.

Henrik Böving said:

I also wonder whether it would be possible to have some compiler flag presets? E.g. basically everything is compiled with -O3 -DNDEBUG

I don't think other languages have presets, but the default should certainly have optimizations disabled.

Francisco Giordano said:

Henrik Böving said:

I also wonder whether it would be possible to have some compiler flag presets? E.g. basically everything is compiled with -O3 -DNDEBUG

I don't think other languages have presets, but the default should certainly have optimizations disabled.

I do agree there should be a no-opt preset as well. It's just that without knowing about the existence of -DNDEBUG you will always get our debug assertions inserted into your code and so the thing you see in godbolt wont be what you see in an average lake build. So it'd be good to communicate to the user somehow that this is somethign they probably want to set if they want to analyze what happens in their real build.
So what is the current compiler optimization level? Can I trust that it's the same as the one I'd get when running lake build?
No, you have to at least pass -O3 -DNDEBUG to get comparable output
